description: Astro Code Minds is a solo operation merging Offensive Security and AI to build next-generation space infrastructure. Focusing on "Medical SOC" concepts, I am developing a tactical telemetry monitoring and anomaly detection system for astronauts. Using Python, FastAPI, and Machine Learning, the goal is to secure and analyze biological and environmental data streams in deep space.
summary: AstroMed SOC is a tactical Medical Security Operations Center built by team AstroCode Minds (Luanda, Angola) to safeguard astronaut health and spacesuit life support (ECLSS) during Extravehicular Activities (EVA) and deep-space missions. Conventional biomedical dashboards passively display sensor curves without verifying data authenticity or correlating gradual multi-sensor drift. Grounded in NASA-STD-3001 and xEMU spacesuit specifications, AstroMed SOC monitors seven real-time physiological and environmental channels across multiple EVA crew profiles. It introduces a Zero Trust telemetry pipeline where every server packet is cryptographically signed with HMAC-SHA256, instantly quarantining tampered or spoofed frames (TAMPERED_DROP) inside a live SIEM audit console. A hybrid detection engine combines deterministic survival guardrails with a multivariate Z-score anomaly index, while a bilingual (EN/PT) Google Gemini Flight Surgeon Copilot provides structured clinical triage and automatically falls back to an offline deterministic engine during deep-space communication blackouts.
details:
OVERVIEW & HOW IT WORKS

During Extravehicular Activities (EVA) and deep-space exploration, astronaut survival depends on continuous biomedical vitals and Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) telemetry. Conventional medical monitoring dashboards passively plot raw sensor numbers without correlating subtle multi-sensor drift or verifying whether incoming telemetry packets are authentic.

AstroMed SOC reimagines aerospace medical monitoring as a tactical Security Operations Center (SOC) operating under Zero Trust principles ("Zero Trust. Always Verify.") across four integrated layers:

1. Real-Time 7-Channel Telemetry Engine: Models Heart Rate (BPM), Blood Oxygen Saturation (SpO2 %), Core Body Temperature (°C), Spacesuit Pressure (kPa), Inspired CO2 (mmHg), Oxygen Reserve (%), and Cumulative Radiation Dose (mSv) calibrated against NASA-STD-3001 human-system standards and xEMU spacesuit operating thresholds across multiple EVA crew profiles.

2. Cryptographic Zero Trust Defense (HMAC-SHA256): Every telemetry frame generated on the backend is cryptographically signed using HMAC-SHA256. When electromagnetic interference or an active telemetry spoofing attack alters vitals in transit, our Quarantine Guard rejects compromised packets immediately (TAMPERED_DROP) and logs the incident in a live SIEM security console so poisoned data never corrupts clinical triage.

3. Hybrid Anomaly Detection Engine: Combines deterministic survival guardrails with a multivariate Z-score anomaly index (0–100) to detect correlated multi-sensor drift—such as gradual suit depressurization or CO2 scrubber degradation—before single-channel thresholds reach fatal limits.

4. Autonomous Flight Surgeon Copilot (Online + Offline Resilience): Powered by the Google Gemini API, the copilot synthesizes verified multi-channel telemetry into structured clinical assessments, root-cause diagnostics, and step-by-step EVA mitigation protocols. Operators can ask live follow-up questions, switch the entire interface and clinical reasoning between English and Portuguese in real time, export forensic JSON incident reports for post-EVA auditing, and rely on an automatic offline deterministic NASA-STD-3001 triage engine during deep-space communication blackouts.

BENEFITS, CREATIVITY & INTENDED IMPACT

By uniting defensive cybersecurity (SIEM telemetry verification) with aerospace clinical decision support, AstroMed SOC prevents both physiological blind spots and cyber-physical data corruption. It prepares autonomous crew medical operations for Artemis lunar surface EVAs and future Mars missions where communication delays of up to 40 minutes make Earth-based real-time monitoring impossible. On Earth, the same architecture directly transfers to remote telemedicine, deep-sea saturation diving, and critical-care intensive care units (ICUs).

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & INFRASTRUCTURE USED

- Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons.

- Backend & Security: Netlify Serverless Functions, Node.js Web Crypto API (HMAC-SHA256 packet signing & verification).

- Artificial Intelligence: Google Gemini API (Flight Surgeon clinical triage & interactive operator chat) paired with a local deterministic rule engine for offline resilience.

- Deployment & Version Control: Git, GitHub, Netlify Cloud Hosting.

FULL VIDEO WALKTHROUGH

Full 2-minute narrated system walkthrough (YouTube): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U9Xe74YLvbM

Public Source Code Repository (GitHub): https://github.com/Israzuba0023/astromed-soc

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) TRANSPARENCY DISCLOSURE

In accordance with NASA Space Apps Challenge SI guidelines:

- Application Feature: Google Gemini LLM is integrated into the AstroMed SOC Flight Surgeon Copilot to generate clinical triage recommendations from verified telemetry.

- Development & Documentation: LLM assistants were used to accelerate TypeScript/React boilerplate structuring and technical documentation review.

- Audio & Media: Text-to-speech SI synthesis was used to generate the English voiceover narration for the demonstration video. No NASA logos, flags, or official branding elements were generated or modified using SI tools.
